[TODAY] 36 years of Hubble: 0.1% of the sky. 🔭

In more than three decades, the Hubble Space Telescope has imaged only about one-tenth of one percent of the sky. NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has a mirror the same size, but each image covers about 100 times more sky. In its first five years, NASA expects Roman to image 50 times as much sky as Hubble did in 30.

Roman launched on Aug. 30. NASA will release its first images on Dec. 7 during a live stream from a science meeting in San Francisco.

Reality check: the images are not public yet; Roman's main surveys are still ahead.

Save this if you want to catch the Dec. 7 reveal.

[EMERGING] You were born making hemoglobin that doesn't sickle.

Early in life, the body makes fetal hemoglobin, which resists the stiff, sickle-shaped red cells behind sickle cell pain crises. Beam Therapeutics' risto-cel edits a patient's own blood stem cells to switch it back on, changing single DNA letters without cutting both strands.

On Nov 10, the company said its pivotal trial met its main goal: freedom from severe pain crises for at least 12 straight months. Of 49 people treated, 31 had reached that follow-up.

Reality check: company topline data; details come in 2027. It still requires chemotherapy and a stem cell transplant. Not medical advice.

[EMERGING] 1.6 million miles, measured finer than an atom. 🛰️

LISA, a mission led by ESA with NASA as a partner, will fly three spacecraft in a triangle 1.6 million miles (2.5 million km) on each side. Lasers will track distance changes smaller than a helium atom: the signature of gravitational waves, ripples in space-time.

Two new NASA-led studies show those ripples could also reveal planets. Pairs of white dwarfs, the dead cores of Sun-like stars, send a steady signal. A big enough planet would make the pair wobble, leaving a pattern in it.

Reality check: launch is planned for the mid-2030s. No planet has yet been found around such a pair.

[EMERGING] How many qubits to crack your bank's encryption? 🔐

RSA-2048 is one of the internet's most used locks, from online banking to email. On Oct 29, quantum company Alice & Bob estimated that a machine of 22,593 of its "cat qubits" could break it in about three days, 40 times fewer qubits than a 2025 Google estimate.

Reality check: this is a company preprint, not yet peer reviewed. It assumes qubits far beyond anything built; the company's largest error-corrected chip has 12. Quantum-safe standards already exist.

[IMAGINE] 28 miles on Mars, steered mostly by itself. 🚙

What's real: on Oct 11, NASA's Perseverance rover reached 28.10 miles (45.22 km), the farthest any vehicle has driven on another world. Opportunity needed almost 15 years to set the old record; Perseverance took five and a half. For over 90% of that distance, its AutoNav system mapped hazards in 3D while rolling and plotted the route between waypoints chosen on Earth.

Its extended mission runs through roughly the end of 2028.

The speculation: what if future rovers scouted whole regions on their own, mapping safe ground before astronauts ever arrive?
